chapters.title: The Blue Planet
chapters.tease: One connected ocean covers 71% of Earth and holds 97% of its water: it sets the climate we all live in.

chapters.title: Where the Water Came From
chapters.tease: Knowing where our water came from tells us whether ocean worlds like Earth could be common.

chapters.title: One World Ocean
chapters.tease: Treating the five oceans as one explains how heat, life and pollution travel around the whole globe.

chapters.title: Why the Sea Is Salty
chapters.tease: Salt sets seawater's density, and density differences drive the currents that stir the whole ocean.

chapters.title: The Shape of the Seafloor
chapters.tease: Seabed maps guide tsunami warnings, cables and fisheries, yet only about a quarter is mapped in detail.

chapters.title: Plate Tectonics and Ocean Basins
chapters.tease: Plate tectonics explains where oceans open and close, and where earthquakes and volcanoes strike.

chapters.title: The Mid-Ocean Ridge
chapters.tease: The ridge builds the ocean floor, and its mirrored magnetic stripes clinched plate tectonics.

chapters.title: Trenches and the Challenger Deep
chapters.tease: Trenches recycle ocean floor into the mantle and spawn the world's greatest earthquakes and tsunamis.

chapters.title: Seamounts and Hotspots
chapters.tease: Hotspot trails record how plates move, and seamounts gather life in the open deep sea.

chapters.title: Sediments: the Ocean's Memory
chapters.tease: Seafloor mud holds the best record of past climate, including warmings like the one we are causing.

chapters.title: How Waves Work
chapters.tease: Waves carry storm energy across whole oceans while the water itself barely moves.

chapters.title: Rogue Waves
chapters.tease: A single laser reading in 1995 proved that the sailors' monster waves were real.

chapters.title: The Tides
chapters.tease: The pull of the Moon and Sun lifts whole oceans twice a day and sets the rhythm of every coast.

chapters.title: Tsunamis
chapters.tease: A sudden jolt of the seabed can send a wave across an ocean at the speed of a jet.

chapters.title: Surface Currents and Gyres
chapters.tease: Winds and the Earth's spin turn the upper ocean into giant wheels that span whole basins.

chapters.title: The Gulf Stream
chapters.tease: A warm current mightier than all the world's rivers shaped trade routes and Europe's climate.

chapters.title: The Global Conveyor Belt
chapters.tease: A planet-wide loop of sinking and rising water stores heat and carbon for a thousand years.

chapters.title: Upwelling
chapters.tease: Wind-driven upwelling turns a few narrow coasts into the most productive waters on Earth.

chapters.title: Eddies and Whirlpools
chapters.tease: Spinning eddies carry heat and life across oceans; tidal whirlpools inspired legends.

chapters.title: El Niño and La Niña
chapters.tease: A seesaw of wind and water across the Pacific reshapes weather, harvests and fisheries worldwide.

chapters.title: The Sunlit Zone
chapters.tease: Almost every meal in the sea starts as sunlight caught in the top 200 metres.

chapters.title: The Twilight Zone
chapters.tease: Every night the biggest migration on Earth climbs hundreds of metres to feed, unseen by almost anyone.

chapters.title: The Midnight Zone
chapters.tease: The biggest habitat on Earth is pitch dark, where three in four animals make their own light.

chapters.title: The Abyss
chapters.tease: Half the planet's surface is cold, dark abyssal plain, and the mining industry has found it.

chapters.title: The Hadal Zone
chapters.tease: Even at the bottom of the deepest trench, 11 km down, animals live, and our pollution reached them first.

chapters.title: Light and Colour Underwater
chapters.tease: The sea is blue because water eats red light first, and deep-sea life has evolved around it.

chapters.title: Pressure
chapters.tease: The deep sea crushes air, not water: understanding that made diving, submarines and deep science possible.

chapters.title: Temperature and the Thermocline
chapters.tease: A warm skin floats on a near-freezing ocean, and that cold deep is now storing our planet's extra heat.

chapters.title: Sound in the Sea
chapters.tease: In the dark sea, sound is the long-range sense: it lets whales talk across basins and us map the floor.

chapters.title: The Polar Oceans
chapters.tease: The poles hold the planet's freezer and its richest summer seas, and both are changing fastest of all.

chapters.title: Plankton: the Drifting Multitude
chapters.tease: Too small to see, plankton feed nearly all sea life and record a changing ocean.

chapters.title: The Breath of the Ocean
chapters.tease: Ocean plankton made the oxygen-rich air we breathe and still do half the planet's photosynthesis.

chapters.title: The Ocean Food Web
chapters.tease: The food web shows where the sea's energy goes and why losing one species can unravel many.

chapters.title: Jellyfish and Their Kin
chapters.tease: Brainless, boneless and older than dinosaurs, jellyfish thrive in seas that humans have disturbed.

chapters.title: Octopus, Squid and Cuttlefish
chapters.tease: Cephalopods evolved big brains and colour-changing skin along a path entirely separate from ours.

chapters.title: Crabs, Lobsters and Krill
chapters.tease: Crustaceans conquered the sea in armour, and Antarctic krill alone feed a continent of wildlife.

chapters.title: The World of Fishes
chapters.tease: Fishes are the most diverse vertebrates on Earth and the wild protein that billions rely on.

chapters.title: Sharks and Rays
chapters.tease: Sharks and rays outlived several mass extinctions but have lost most of their ocean numbers since 1970.

chapters.title: Sea Turtles
chapters.tease: Sea turtles navigate by magnetism, but warming sand now tips their hatchlings towards all-female.

chapters.title: Seabirds
chapters.tease: Seabirds fly and dive to extremes that test the limits of a bird's body, and warn us when the sea fails.

chapters.title: Whales
chapters.tease: Whales show evolution in action: land mammals that became the largest, deepest-diving animals alive.

chapters.title: The Blue Whale
chapters.tease: The largest animal ever known shows how far the ocean can push body size, and how fast we can undo it.

chapters.title: Dolphins and Porpoises
chapters.tease: Dolphins see with sound and live in cultures of their own, yet some species are down to a handful.

chapters.title: Seals, Sea Lions and Walruses
chapters.tease: Pinnipeds dive deeper than submarines on a single breath and now carry sensors where ships cannot go.

chapters.title: The Giant Squid
chapters.tease: The giant squid shows how a sea monster became a real animal through specimens, cameras and patience.

chapters.title: Bioluminescence
chapters.tease: In the largest habitat on Earth, most light comes from living things, and it lit up modern biology too.

chapters.title: Great Ocean Migrations
chapters.tease: Ocean migrants cross whole basins on hidden maps, and their journeys tie the fate of distant coasts together.

chapters.title: Life at Hydrothermal Vents
chapters.tease: Vents proved that whole ecosystems can run on chemical energy from the Earth instead of sunlight.

chapters.title: Whale Falls
chapters.tease: One dead whale feeds a deep-sea community for decades and revealed hundreds of species new to science.

chapters.title: Living Fossils
chapters.tease: Living fossils show which body plans can outlast mass extinctions, and one may help keep our medicines safe.

chapters.title: Where Land Meets Sea
chapters.tease: Coasts are where the sea reshapes the land fastest, and where two in five people now live.

chapters.title: Beaches and Sand
chapters.tease: Sand looks endless, yet beaches are moving rivers of grains and the world is mining them faster than rivers refill them.

chapters.title: Rocky Shores and Tide Pools
chapters.tease: A strip of wet rock gave ecology its clearest experiments, and the idea of the keystone species.

chapters.title: Estuaries and Salt Marshes
chapters.tease: Where rivers meet the tide, brackish shallows raise much of the sea's fish and feed migrating birds.

chapters.title: Mangrove Forests
chapters.tease: Trees that live in salt water shield coasts from storms and lock away carbon in their mud.

chapters.title: Kelp Forests
chapters.tease: Kelp forests showed how one predator, the sea otter, can decide whether a coast has a forest or bare rock.

chapters.title: Seagrass Meadows
chapters.tease: Underwater meadows of flowering plants feed dugongs and bury carbon faster than most forests.

chapters.title: Coral Reefs
chapters.tease: Tiny polyps and their algae build reefs that shelter about a quarter of known marine species.

chapters.title: The Great Barrier Reef
chapters.tease: The largest structure built by life, seen from orbit, is now a record of how fast the ocean is warming.

chapters.title: Islands and Atolls
chapters.tease: Islands are evolution's laboratories, from Darwin's Galápagos to newborn Surtsey and the low Maldives.

chapters.title: The Polynesian Wayfinders
chapters.tease: Polynesian navigators found the far-flung islands of the largest ocean by reading stars, swells and birds.

chapters.title: Ships of the Age of Sail
chapters.tease: Sailing ships knitted the continents together, and their routes followed the planet's great wind belts.

chapters.title: Finding Longitude
chapters.tease: Solving longitude turned the open ocean from a guessing game into a grid ships could navigate safely.

chapters.title: Captain Cook's Pacific
chapters.tease: Cook's charts finished the outline of the Pacific, and opened its islands to empire, trade and disease.

chapters.title: The Challenger Expedition
chapters.tease: One ship's four-year voyage turned the deep sea from a blank on the map into a science.

chapters.title: Diving: Bells to Scuba
chapters.tease: Learning to carry air underwater opened the shallow sea to salvage, science and millions of divers.

chapters.title: Submarines
chapters.tease: Submarines turned the sea's interior into a hiding place, and nuclear power let them stay down for months.

chapters.title: The Deepest Dive
chapters.tease: Reaching the Challenger Deep proved humans could survive the ocean's greatest pressure, and return.

chapters.title: Mapping the Seafloor
chapters.tease: Seafloor maps revealed the mid-ocean ridge, clinched plate tectonics and still guide cables, ships and science.

chapters.title: Robots, Floats and Satellites
chapters.tease: Robots, floats and satellites now take the ocean's pulse every day, from the surface to 6,000 metres.

chapters.title: Fishing Through the Ages
chapters.tease: Fish fed humanity before farming did, and industrial nets have since emptied whole seas.

chapters.title: Shipping and World Trade
chapters.tease: The humble steel box made distance cheap and turned the ocean into the world's conveyor belt.

chapters.title: Ports and Harbours
chapters.tease: Ports turned sheltered water into cities, and they keep moving seaward as ships grow.

chapters.title: Pirates and Privateers
chapters.tease: Pirates tested who rules the sea, and every age has had to answer them again.

chapters.title: Shipwrecks
chapters.tease: Wrecks freeze a single day in time, preserving ships, cargoes and lives no archive recorded.

chapters.title: Lighthouses and Safe Passage
chapters.tease: Lighthouses turned deadly coasts into charted landmarks, each with its own coded flash.

chapters.title: Sea Power
chapters.tease: Navies decided empires, from Athenian oars to carrier aircraft, by ruling the sea lanes.

chapters.title: Who Owns the Ocean
chapters.tease: A 1982 treaty divided the ocean into zones, deciding who may fish, drill and sail where.

chapters.title: Farming the Sea
chapters.tease: Farms now supply more seafood than wild fisheries, reshaping coasts from Norway to China.

chapters.title: Energy from the Ocean
chapters.tease: Offshore rigs fuelled the twentieth century; offshore wind and tides may power the next.

chapters.title: The Ocean Thermostat
chapters.tease: The sea has absorbed about nine tenths of global warming, sparing the air but storing trouble for centuries.

chapters.title: The Ocean Carbon Sink
chapters.tease: The ocean pulls about a quarter of our carbon dioxide out of the air each year, slowing climate change.

chapters.title: A Warming Ocean
chapters.tease: Thousands of robot floats now show the ocean gaining heat year after year, pushing sea life toward the poles.

chapters.title: Rising Seas
chapters.tease: A rise of about 20 centimetres since 1900 already decides which tides flood cities and islands.

chapters.title: Ocean Acidification
chapters.tease: The CO₂ the sea absorbs is turning seawater more acidic and stripping shell builders of their raw material.

chapters.title: Coral Bleaching
chapters.tease: Marine heat is breaking the ancient pact between corals and algae, emptying reefs worldwide.

chapters.title: Melting Sea Ice
chapters.tease: Shrinking Arctic ice turns a reflective lid into dark water that absorbs heat and speeds warming.

chapters.title: Hurricanes and Typhoons
chapters.tease: Warm seawater powers the planet's most destructive storms, and a warmer ocean makes them stronger and wetter.

chapters.title: Marine Heatwaves
chapters.tease: Months-long ocean heatwaves are collapsing kelp forests, fisheries and seabird colonies within a few seasons.

chapters.title: Dead Zones
chapters.tease: Fertiliser run-off suffocates coastal seas, yet the Black Sea shows dead zones can come back to life.

chapters.title: Overfishing
chapters.tease: The Grand Banks cod collapse of 1992 showed that even the richest fishery on Earth can be emptied in a lifetime.

chapters.title: Plastic Seas
chapters.tease: Ocean gyres gather the world's floating plastic, which breaks into microplastics that reach every depth.

chapters.title: Oil Spills
chapters.tease: Each great spill, from Cornwall to Alaska to the Gulf of Mexico, rewrote the rules for carrying and drilling oil.

chapters.title: A Noisier, Brighter Sea
chapters.tease: Ship noise, sonar and coastal lights now drown the sounds and darkness that marine life relies on.

chapters.title: Hitchhikers and Invaders
chapters.tease: Ships, canals and aquariums move marine species across the planet, and a few invaders reshape whole seas.

chapters.title: Marine Protected Areas
chapters.tease: Fully protected reserves let fish grow big and plentiful, and the surplus spills over to feed nearby fisheries.

chapters.title: Bringing Reefs and Kelp Back
chapters.tease: Coral nurseries, urchin culls, oyster reefs and seagrass seeding show that lost marine habitats can be rebuilt.

chapters.title: The High Seas Treaty
chapters.tease: The 2023 High Seas Treaty gave the two-thirds of the ocean beyond any country's control a way to be protected.

chapters.title: Deep-Sea Mining
chapters.tease: Battery metals lie in nodules on the deep seabed, but mining them could scar ecosystems we have barely seen.

chapters.title: The Ocean's Future
chapters.tease: Recovering whales and new global treaties show the ocean can heal when people give it the chance.
